title: Call interface: error taxonomy, schema authoring guidance, and user-facing diagnostics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: produce a pragmatic, implementation-friendly guidance doc and runtime error taxonomy for function/tool calling that (1) standardizes the JSON-schema authoring style we accept, (2) defines deterministic coercion and validation behavior, and (3) specifies stable, localizable error codes and messages for SDKs, Console, and API responses. This ticket covers the spec, examples, diagnostic UX requirements, and a rollout plan (feature-flagged). It excludes runtime kernel-level optimizations; those are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: A stable spec doc exists that prescribes: schema versioning header, allowed JSON Schema subset, required vs optional semantics, and coercion rules (strict and permissive modes).
A documented error taxonomy with unique error codes and recommended HTTP mappings is published and reviewed by SDK and Console owners.
Runtime behavior for strict vs permissive validation is implemented behind a feature flag and covered by unit/integration tests.
SDK surface (JS/Python) renders messages according to localization and ergonomic rules; Console displays diagnostic links and example failing payloads.
Migration guidance for existing tool schemas is created, including a compatibility shim that can be enabled per-namespace.
Telemetry events (validation.result, validation.coercion, validation.error_code) are emitted and documented for SRE/observability teams.
technical_notes: We intentionally accept a limited JSON Schema subset (core: type, properties, required, enum, minimum/maximum, pattern, items with single subschema). No 'allOf/anyOf/oneOf' in initial phase to avoid ambiguous validation paths.
Schema authoring should include a schema metadata block: {"x-schema-version": "2026-01", "x-authoring-guidelines": "redwood:strict-by-default"}. We recommend namespacing custom keywords with 'x-'.

Two validation modes: strict (reject on type mismatch, missing required) and permissive (attempt deterministic coercion then validate). Default mode = strict for public hosted tenants; permissive available as opt-in flag for legacy compatibility.

Deterministic coercion rules: booleans: allow 'true'/'false' (string) -> boolean; numbers: parse numeric strings unless contains non-numeric chars; arrays: single values can be wrapped into single-element array if schema expects array and 'x-coerce-single-to-array' is true.
Validation should produce a canonical error structure with fields: code, path, human_readable, hint, example_fix. All fields are strings for downstream ingestion.
error_taxonomy: MALFORMED_PAYLOAD: input not valid JSON or not parseable.
SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH: schema declares an unsupported or higher x-schema-version.
MISSING_REQUIRED: a required property is absent.
TYPE_MISMATCH: value type does not match schema type after attempted coercion.
ENUM_MISMATCH: value not one of allowed enum values.
COERCION_FAILED: type coercion was attempted but could not convert value deterministically.
EXTRA_PROPERTIES: received properties not described in schema (treated as warning in permissive mode, error in strict mode).
PATTERN_MISMATCH: string failed regex pattern constraint.
NUMERIC_BOUNDS: number outside minimum/maximum when strict validation applied.
runtime_behavior: HTTP mapping suggestion: 400 for client-side validation errors (MALFORMED_PAYLOAD, MISSING_REQUIRED, TYPE_MISMATCH), 422 for semantic validation (ENUM_MISMATCH, PATTERN_MISMATCH), 428 for schema version mismatch with migration hint.
When permissive mode performs coercion, emit validation.coercion telemetry with original and coerced string values (redact PII).
Console will surface an expandable diagnostic with: failing payload, repeater to re-run with permissive mode enabled, and link to schema authoring docs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (spec+doc): publish spec and examples. Notify SDK/Console teams and create RFC PR for review (feature gated).
Phase 2 (server+telemetry): implement validation pipeline + telemetry, run Dark Traffic against dedicated staging models for 2 weeks to collect mismatches.
Phase 3 (gradual opt-in): enable permissive compatibility shim for selected tenants/namespaces and monitor error rates and SLO impact.
Phase 4 (default strict): after 6 weeks and successful migrations, flip default to strict for new schemas and announce deprecation window for old behavior.
test_plan: Unit tests covering each error code path with canonical JSON-pointer paths asserted.
Integration tests where SDKs send both well-formed and intentionally malformed payloads; assert API error codes and telemetry events.
End-to-end dark-traffic run to measure how many existing calls would be rejected under strict mode and to collect top offending schemas for migration guidance.
Localization tests to ensure messages are replaceable and codes remain stable across locales.
